newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt issuers pile into new issue bandwagon.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt issuers pile into new issue bandwagon.

text.p: Corporate debt issuers are piling on the new issue bandwagon as lower interest rates pave the way to cheaper financing, dealers said.
"The tone in the market continues to be very good...we continue to see a lot of opportunistic issuers in here," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Adding to the growing list of new names is Harcourt General Inc, which is expected to issue a $500 million three-part debt deal via Salomon Brothers, dealers said.
The offering is expected to have 10-, 30- and 100-year tranches, according to dealers.
The publishing company currently has $750 million in shelf debt filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures and working capital requirements, as well as to reduce outstanding debt.
Another name that emerged in Tuesday's business is Chase Manhattan Corp. The bank is expected to issue $250 million two-year notes via Chase Securities, dealers said.
Commercical Metals is circulating the primary arena as a potential debt issuer as well, players said.
Meanwhile, Avon Products Inc is said to be eyeing the private placement market to issue a 10-year 144a offering, players added.
The latest deals will join a growing list of other opportunistic issuers already queued up to come to market.

Delaware-based Hercules Inc, a global producer of chemicals and related products, is slated to bring $100 million three-year notes and $100 million 30-year debt with a 10-year put option, syndicate players said.
JP Morgan Securities and NationsBanc Capital Markets are expected to underwrite the offering, players said.
Among other high-grade offerings is Brunswick Corp's $200 million Baa1/BBB-plus rated 30-year debt via Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal will incluse a Treasury make-whole call provision.

Quebecor Printing, a unit of Quebecor Inc, is expected to bring a $150 million 30-year debt offering, putable in seven-years, via Salomon Brothers, sources said. Quebecor, is a leading commercial printer in Canada and Europee and the second largest in the United States.
Among other high-grade issues, Taubman Realty is said to be readying a $100 million 10-year debt deal via Merrill Lynch, players said.
IES Industries is planning a $135 million 12-year issue via competitive bid on Wednesday, sources said.
Investment-grade issuance is not expected to let up as Raytheon Co's jumbo $2.5 billion debt offering via Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is expected next week, players said.
A big week is also on tap for the high-yield sector, as underwriters get set to bring about 18 new junk bond deals, totalling $3.0 billion, this week, players said.
Primus Telecommunications Group's $125 million seven-year notes is expected via Lehman Brothers. Price talk on the issue is seen between 11.50 and 11.75 percent, sources said.
Marsh Supermarkets is slated to bring $150 million 10-year 144a notes through Merrill Lynch. Price talk is for 275 to 300 basis points over comparable Tresuries.

Jakarta-based Tjiwi Kimia Finance Mauritus Ltd, the Indonesian paper firm, is slated to bring $400 million seven-year senior unsecurd 144a notes via Goldman Sachs. Price talk is for 400 basis points over Treasuries, players said.

Others include Golden Ocean Group Ltd's $150 million, Decisionone Corp's $150 million, Hollywood Park's $125 million, Hollywood Theatre's $100 million and Price Communications Cellular Holdings' $80 million (proceeds) deals, syndicate players said.
The steady pace of debt issuance is expected to continue because an attractive interest rate environment is still luring spectators into the primary debt arena.
Currently, the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is 6.41 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
